title: The Foundation: Stones of Divine Craftsmanship
english: But not even this stone is natural; for in no way did they cut the column from the peak of a wild rock, a long span measure of the path. But the whole shines with skillful works and has a shifting nature, glittering with radiance. For the wheel turns round perpetually, as it were, with equal circles endless; but the wheels' shallow uncoil their coils. There is, on the one hand, to see the red ochre mixed; on the other, a fine light to mortal eyes like groanings. Elsewhere the gleam rushed toward the bright silver, imitating at rest the image of boxwood or of beeswax honey; which men cleanse with pure pourings, wiping many times with wool under the sun's rays; which, passing over, turns to silver, yet not yet has it turned the whole color, still showing golden remnants. Such also is the long elephant dyed with drag-ropes, the silver color of yesteryear driving upon the apple. In what part does it have grace? For in no way did that nature leave its dark color, but it mixed the well-written crafted works of stone.

Yes indeed, not even this stone is polished; for in no way did they cut the column from the peak of a wild rock, a long span measure of the path. But the whole shines with skillful works and has a shifting nature, glittering with radiance. title: The Ambo Platform: Octagonal Form and Marble Columns
english: The ambo stands octagonal in form, rising in graceful stages to a height befitting the proclamation of the divine word. Its columns are of precious marble, green as the sea, and its capitals are carved with the vine and the cross. Upon its parapets are silver discs, chased with the figures of the prophets and the apostles, each bearing his symbol. In the center, above the place where the deacon stands, the cross blazes in gold and gems, the sign of our salvation.

From the ambo the deacon cries aloud the Gospel, and his voice is carried on the air to every corner of the great church, as though the dome itself were a great ear listening to the word of God. The light from the lamps above falls upon the reader, making a crown of light about his head.

title: Conclusion: The Ambo as Cosmic Liturgy
english: Thus the ambo stands complete, a wonder of the age, a crown of the church, a harbor of light for those who sail the stormy seas of this life. Its form is octagonal, its columns of precious marble, its capitals carved with the vine and the cross, its parapets adorned with silver discs bearing the prophets and apostles. In the center the cross blazes in gold and gems, the sign of our salvation.

Here the deacon cries aloud the Gospel, and his voice is carried on the air to every corner of the great church, as though the dome itself were a great ear listening to the word of God. The sacred light cheers all: even the sailor guiding his bark on the waves, leaving behind him the unfriendly billows of the raging Pontus, and winding a sinuous course amidst creeks and rocks, with heart fearful at the dangers of his nightly wanderings — does not guide his laden vessel by the light of Cynosure, or the circling Bear, but by the divine light of the church itself. Yet not only does it guide the merchant at night, like the rays from the Pharos on the coast of Africa, but it also shows the way to the living God.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
